image.name: Valley Cold Storage & Transportation
image.description: Valley Cold Storage & Transportation owns and operates temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics infrastructure serving food, agriculture and distribution customers in southern New Mexico, west Texas and northern Mexico. The business was established in 2008 and operates cold-storage facilities in Las Cruces and Santa Teresa. Ridgewood Infrastructure completed a founder-led recapitalization in Q4 2024. Clay Bush and Jennifer Bush continue to be identified by the company as owners; all current percentage stakes, the Ridgewood fund and the acquisition SPV are not publicly disclosed.

image.name: Crosslake Fibre
image.description: Crosslake Fibre owns and operates long-haul subsea and terrestrial fiber systems serving carriers, hyperscalers, financial institutions and enterprises across North America and Europe. Its two named live systems span approximately 681 km: the Lake Ontario route linking Toronto, Buffalo and New York, and the CrossChannel route linking Slough and Paris. The company reports more than 25 backbone points of presence plus separate extranet reach; extranet sites are not treated as owned PoPs. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund II invested in December 2017 and remains the current sponsor identified by both Tiger and Crosslake. Two Fund II AIVs held a 93.26% indirect interest as of August 10, 2018, while the current ownership percentage is not publicly disclosed. No later sale or signed sponsor transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Danskammer Energy
image.description: Danskammer Energy, LLC owns and operates a 532 MW, four-unit natural-gas-fired generating station in Newburgh, New York that supplies energy, capacity and ancillary services to NYISO. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund II led the acquisition that closed on December 27, 2017 and retained voting control through Danskammer Investments LLC; the bankruptcy schedules attribute 81.79% of HoldCo shares to that vehicle, while the economics among Tiger affiliates are not publicly disclosed. The company entered Chapter 11 on June 10, 2026 and continued operating as a debtor-in-possession and NYISO interim service provider while pursuing a Section 363 sale. No buyer, completed sale, permanent retirement or Tiger exit was public by August 19, 2026. The separate proposed Energy Center repowering was denied, its applications were withdrawn in 2024, and it was not built.
